Subject: Post-call: Inference A/B benchmarking plan & p95/p99 targets

Sam — thanks again for the thoughtful conversation earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment before we start tests:

- Goal: A/B comparison of Redwood-hosted inference vs Hyperscaler-X managed inference for your production-like workload. Focus metrics: latency (p95, p99), sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and tail behavior under burst.
- Workloads to test: 1) short responses (~64 tokens) 2) long context (4k tokens) 3) mixed realtime burst (50–200 qps).
- Success signals: p95 under 120ms for short requests; p99 sufficient for SLO analysis (we'll provide raw logs).

Proposed plan:
1) Redwood provides a test harness + config (we'll include a detailed plan and attachments)
2) Run three independent A/B runs (30m each) for reproducibility
3) Deliver granular token-level latency CSVs + aggregated p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec by minute

Can you confirm: (a) the staging endpoints we should target, (b) whether we have permission to run load against those endpoints during the Feb 23–25 window, and (c) any additional metrics you want instrumented (GPU utilization, queue depth)?

We'll share a formal test plan shortly (Marissa is prepping it). If that window doesn't work, propose a few alternatives.

— Rafael

Hi all — attaching the test plan and a quickstart for our benchmark harness. Highlights below; see attachments for full configs and the workload generator scripts.

What we'll run
- A/B runs comparing: Redwood-hosted (pinned model v1.14, 4-bit quant) vs Hyperscaler-X endpoint (their default infra).
- Payloads: short (30–80 tokens), medium (512 tokens), long (4k and 8k).
- Runs: 3x 30-minute runs per workload, cold-start at start of each run, 10-minute warmup excluded from metrics.

Metrics collected
- Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 per-second + per-token breakdown
- Throughput: tokens/sec per GPU/minute
- Resource: GPU util, host CPU, memory, queue lengths, and tokenization time

Notes and caveats
- Tokenization: we'll run tokenization locally to normalize overhead and also capture per-request tokenizer time so we can subtract that for model-only latency when needed.
- Reproducibility: we'll seed RNGs and record exact model hashes.

Attachments:
- [Attachment: acro_ab_test_plan.pdf (PDF, 92KB)]
- [Attachment: redwood-benchmark-quickstart.md (Markdown, 7KB)]

- Sam: confirm the 8k addition as requested.
- Rafael: if OK, I'll schedule the jobs and share links to the live dashboards.

— Marissa

Quick tech notes from my side — a few things to ensure the numbers are comparable and actionable:

1) Harness: prefer replay of sampled production traffic where possible (keeps burst patterns realistic). If you provide logs we can convert them to the harness format; otherwise synthetic distribution ok for preliminary runs.
2) Concurrency and warmup: run 3x 30m as planned but with 10m ramp, then 30m steady-state capture. We'll run 3 different concurrency levels (50, 250, 1000 req/s) to map the knee.
3) p95/p99 calc: we'll compute these from raw per-request end-to-end times and also from per-token extrapolation. For long-context (8k) we must track KV cache growth and measure tokens/sec decline over time.
4) Environment: ask AcroSoft to ensure staging doesn't have request-level prioritization or gateway caching; otherwise we'll see artificial improvements.

Commands (example harness):
- ./benchmark run --config acro_ab_test_plan.yaml --output out/run1 --seed 42
- ./benchmark analyze --input out/run1/logs --metrics latency,tokens_per_sec --percentiles 50,90,95,99

I'll join the run kickoff and monitor GPU metrics in real time.

— Dev Patel
